description: A pure CALCULATION node — ALL eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a SYMMETRIC matrix by cyclic Jacobi rotation. Matrix in, values + vectors out; draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: a symmetric matrix as JSON in, its complete eigen-decomposition out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

WHY IT IS A NODE AND NOT A FLOW. Jacobi repeats until the off-diagonal mass drops below tolerance — a data-dependent stopping test. The flow evaluator is a DAG (topological sort, cycles rejected), so no arrangement of nodes can express that loop; the Loop node is a geometry array and does not iterate values. Unrolling power-iteration blocks in the graph works but only ever yields the DOMINANT pair, and converges at |λ₂/λ₁| per block. This runs the loop internally, converges in 2–4 sweeps, and returns every pair.

INPUT: wire a square symmetric matrix into valin-matrix — an inertia tensor, a covariance matrix, a stiffness matrix, or a graph Laplacian. The matrix is symmetrised on entry ((A + Aᵀ)/2), so float noise or a slightly-off typed tensor is well-posed rather than silently wrong. NON-SYMMETRIC input is therefore treated as its symmetric part — this node does not do general (complex) eigenvalues.

OUTPUTS:
• `val-values` — the eigenvalues as an n×1 column, sorted (default largest first).
• `val-vectors` — an n×n matrix whose COLUMNS are the matching unit eigenvectors, in the same order. They are orthonormal, so the transpose is also the inverse.
• `val-dominant` — the leading eigenvector alone, as an n×1 column, ready to wire onward.
• `val-angle` — the direction of the leading eigenvector in the XY plane, in DEGREES. For a 2×2 tensor this is the principal-axis angle directly.

WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN depends on the matrix you feed it. Inertia tensor [[Ixx, −Ixy], [−Ixy, Iyy]] → I_max / I_min and the principal-axis angle, which is what governs bending of any unsymmetric section (angles, channels, Z-purlins). Covariance of a point set → PCA: the leading eigenvector is the shape's dominant orientation. Stiffness with mass → mode shapes. Graph Laplacian → the second-smallest eigenvalue's vector is the Fiedler vector, which partitions the graph.

Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
